clue.text: Hawker's Car Elevator at bargain price

parts.note: something sold at a bargain price is cheap
a jack is the device that lifts a car to change a wheel

explanation.surface: A street seller is flogging a car lift at a knockdown price.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Hawker stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapjack is a pedlar of shoddy goods, a street seller who cries his wares.

clue.text: State supports first form providing such education

definitions.text: State supports first form providing such education

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: a school's first form can be called Class I, written as letters plus the Roman numeral
CAL is a short form for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A school whose state-funded first form offers a traditional grounding in Latin and Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supports' puts CAL below CLASS I. The whole clue also describes the answer: a first form offering a grounding in Latin and Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical education is one built on the study of Latin and Greek, as old grammar schools offered from the first form.

clue.text: Jane takes one in a bird's nest

indicators.note: Jane taking a letter in means it goes inside her surname

parts.note: Jane Eyre is the heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Jane, the novel's heroine, settles into a bird's nest.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane is not a definition but Charlotte Bronte's heroine, giving her surname EYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the high, remote nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: Old parrot inviting another bird to pay a call

parts.note: to pop in is to pay a brief call on someone
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: An elderly parrot asks a second bird round for a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inviting' and 'to' are link words; the pieces come in answer order, POP IN then JAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Popinjay is an archaic word for a parrot, now used mainly for a vain, chattering person.

clue.text: Whitefriars sanctuary — name of a dog!

explanation.surface: A London sanctuary district is said to be named after a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitefriars, a district of old London, was a sanctuary for debtors and criminals known as Alsatia; its refugees were called by the adjective formed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsatia was the cant name of the Whitefriars sanctuary, so one sheltering there was so called; the same word is a British name for a German shepherd dog.

clue.text: Destiny with which king is satisfied

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
a demand that is met has been satisfied

explanation.surface: Fate is whatever a contented monarch accepts.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is a Turkish word, from Arabic, for fate or the will of Allah.

clue.text: Disreputable notice inserted in short

indicators.note: the notice is placed inside the word for short, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to be shy of a sum is to be short of it
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A dodgy advertisement slipped in briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A shady character is of doubtful honesty, someone not quite respectable.

clue.text: Robust sheep may have this complaint

explanation.surface: A strong sheep can still catch this disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy means strong and robust; it is also the name of gid, a brain disease of sheep that makes them stagger.

clue.text: His income derived from an eccentric aunt with tin?

definitions.text: His income derived from an eccentric aunt with tin?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre or odd, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; tin is also slang for money

explanation.surface: A man lives off the money left him by a dotty, wealthy aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges AN AUNT TIN; the whole clue also describes the answer, since tin is slang for money and an annuity is income bought with it.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuitant receives a yearly payment, an annuity, often bought or bequeathed by a relative.

clue.text: Servitude imposed on many a countryman

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece imposed on another sits above it

parts.note: the yoke is a symbol of servitude or bondage
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Bondage forced on many a rural worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many a' looks like a phrase, but 'many' gives L and 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is a rustic, an unsophisticated person from the country.

clue.text: Milton's blind fury (sic) with th' abhorred shears

definitions.text: Milton's blind fury (sic) with th' abhorred shears

parts.words: Milton's blind fury (sic) with th' abhorred shears
parts.note: quotes Milton's Lycidas, where 'the blind Fury with th'abhorred shears' slits life's thread; '(sic)' admits Milton meant a Fate, not a Fury

explanation.surface: A line from Milton about a blind avenger wielding shears.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth three Fates spin, measure and cut the thread of life; Milton called the cutter a Fury, hence the setter's '(sic)'.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropos was the Fate who cut the thread of each mortal's life with her shears.

clue.text: Circumterrestrial bleeper whose variegated skin appears out of place

indicators.note: the shuffled skin sits outside the other piece, wrapped around it
variegated means multicoloured or mixed, so the letters of skin are mixed up

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A beeping satellite is the odd one out among skin-patterned animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin' sounds like the animal's coat but is just fodder; 'appears' is a link, and the satellite's beeps explain the definition 'bleeper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik 1, launched in 1957, was the first artificial satellite to circle the Earth, famous for its radio beeps.

clue.text: The Wild Goose forms part of this — some yarn!

definitions.text: The Wild Goose forms part of this

explanation.surface: A wild goose belongs to a story that is a bit of a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is a flock of wild geese in flight, and also a loosely coiled length of yarn or thread.

clue.text: Teacher's beginning to study the economist — tedious task

indicators.note: the beginning of teacher's is just its opening letter

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
John Stuart Mill was a Victorian economist and philosopher

explanation.surface: A teacher starting to read an economist finds it a grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a monotonous routine, from the wheel once trodden as a punishment.

clue.text: Players not at home in Robinson Crusoe, for example

parts.note: the players in a production are its cast
someone away is not at home

explanation.surface: Actors on tour in a production of Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players not at home' suggests a touring company or away team, but it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe, Defoe's hero, is the classic example of a shipwrecked man stranded on an island.

clue.text: Times can change with onset of science that's meaningful

definitions.text: Times can change with onset of science that's meaningful

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of times and can are to be rearranged
the onset of science is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper can shift its ground once science begins to make sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges TIMES CAN into SEMANTIC, and 'onset of' adds the S from science. The whole clue also points to the answer, the science of meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the branch of linguistics concerned with meaning in words and sentences.

clue.text: Bridge player has a condition — one that needs to be adopted?

definitions.text: one that needs to be adopted?

parts.note: W is West, one of the four players at bridge
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A card player admits to a condition and asks to be taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a homeless, neglected child, the kind who needs taking in by a new family.

clue.text: Stuffing at police get-together, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and only its sound matters

parts.note: a meeting of the police force could be called a force meet

explanation.surface: Stuffing served at a police social, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link; 'say' turns 'force meet' into the identical-sounding stuffing.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcemeat is finely minced, seasoned meat used as a stuffing for poultry.

clue.text: Retaliation for damage to a spire accepted by both sides

indicators.note: the scrambled piece is taken in between the two side letters

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two sides

indicators.note: damage to the words a spire means their letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Two factions agree a reprisal for vandalism to a church spire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage to' scrambles A SPIRE into EPRISA, and 'accepted by' puts it between R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation, paying back an injury in kind.

clue.text: We raise a hardy annual perhaps among legendary monsters

definitions.note: plural in the clue; 'among' says the answer is one of them

indicators.note: raise in the sense of stir up or rouse, so the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: a hardy annual is a kind of garden plant in bloom, hence a flower

explanation.surface: Gardeners grow a tough annual plant among figures of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower has to be found before its letters are mixed with WE, an indirect anagram older Times puzzles allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf is a man of folklore who turns into a wolf at the full moon.

clue.text: Sort of stone fruit?

explanation.surface: A question about some kind of stone fruit, such as a plum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone fruit' reads as one botanical term, like a plum or cherry, but it splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sort of stone, and a lime is a small green citrus fruit.

clue.text: Sees "term" as a sort of definition

definitions.text: Sees "term" as a sort of definition

indicators.note: a sort of signals the letters of sees and term sorted into another order

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry glosses a word as one kind of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges SEES TERM, and the whole clue also says the answer means a term.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is an academic term, one of two half-year divisions of a college year.

clue.text: German coding machine presenting game in new form

indicators.note: putting the words into a new form means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A wartime cipher device turned into a puzzle game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enigma was the cipher device used by German forces in the Second World War, broken at Bletchley Park.

clue.text: Beetle, namely, on a horse .

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A beetle, to be exact, riding on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Where plate-layers work on the railway

definitions.text: Where plate-layers work on the railway

parts.words: Where plate-layers work on the railway
parts.note: plate-layers are railway track workers, but here they are waiters setting out plates in a carriage of a train

explanation.surface: Asks where the gangs who lay railway track do their job.
explanation.walkthrough: On British railways a plate-layer maintains the track; the clue reads the word literally, as someone laying plates on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining car is the railway carriage where meals are served at laid tables.

clue.text: Such courage shown by a man of spirit

definitions.text: Such courage shown by a man of spirit

parts.words: Such courage shown by a man of spirit
parts.note: bravery found in a bottle of gin, which the Netherlands is known for, and a native of the Netherlands

explanation.surface: Describes the bravery displayed by a spirited man.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'man of spirit' sounds brave, but it is a drinker, or a man from the land of gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage bolstered by alcohol is called after the people of the Netherlands, long associated with gin.

clue.text: Name of a Spanish article you found in Germany

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
Sie is the polite German word for you

explanation.surface: A Spanish thing's name that you came across in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's name, a pet form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: Neck shows singular scar

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a scar is a steep rocky outcrop, as is a crag

explanation.surface: A neck bears a lone scar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scar' suggests a wound, but in northern English it is a rocky cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag is the bony end of a neck of mutton, and slang for a person's neck.

clue.text: One trying to catch child's horse, pressed by Miss Oakley

indicators.note: catching something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a trier is someone who tries
gee-gee is childish talk for a horse, written GG

explanation.surface: A pupil tries to catch a pony while the sharpshooter Miss Oakley pushes.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie Oakley was the American Wild West sharpshooter, so what she pressed was on her gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trigger is the lever a shooter squeezes to fire a gun, as the markswoman did.

clue.text: Cat's swell, receiving company

indicators.note: the swell receives the company, taking it inside itself

parts.note: a surge is a swell of the sea

explanation.surface: A cat is fine, and it entertains guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Cat stands for 'is'. 'Cat' is no pet but the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip used for flogging, and a scourge is a whip.

clue.text: Leg-wear a prophet shows

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights worn on the legs

explanation.surface: A prophet displays his stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: In which truth is momentarily revealed

definitions.text: In which truth is momentarily revealed

parts.words: In which truth is momentarily revealed
parts.note: plays on 'the moment of truth', the final sword thrust in a Spanish arena, read as a brief glimpse of truth

explanation.surface: Describes an event that briefly shows the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The moment of truth' is the bullfighting term for the kill; the clue reads it as a fleeting revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Spanish corrida the matador's killing stroke is called the moment of truth.
